_note: What Kaede, who keeps the village shrine, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items her own answers to an omamori and to dishes. Mornings at the shrine she talks of the sweeping. The birthday lines (fall 4), the close lines from band 4, the rite lines once her band 5 scene is seen (heart_kaede_5), the dear lines at band 6 once her band 6 scene is (heart_kaede_6) until she is promised; engaged_ lines once she said yes to the knot, and married (married_kaede) help_ lines on a morning she did a chore, wed_morning_ / wed_evening_ at the farmhouse and wed_out_ elsewhere (data/marriage.json). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Blossom Day is the shrine's busiest morning. I've swept the same petals four times. They keep coming back.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: All the lanterns are lit. If you look up the shrine steps, you'd think the gods were having a party too.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I set out the moon dumplings myself this year. Thirteen of them. Don't count them, one might be missing.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Midnight, and then the first bell of the year. My hands are shaking. Tome says that's how you know you care.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Twice in one day? The fox statues are starting to talk about you.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Still here? Then hold the dustpan. A shrine is mostly sweeping, really.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Oh! You're the new farmer. I'm Kaede. I keep the shrine, or I'm learning to. Grandma Tome keeps me.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: If you ever hear footsteps on the gravel at night, it's only the fox. Probably.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Rain on the shrine roof sounds like a hundred tiny drums. I fold charms at home and listen.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Morning! Mind the gravel, I raked it into waves. Very serious waves.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Grandfather swept this gravel every morning for forty years. I'm on year two. My back already knows.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Snow on the shrine roof is pretty until you have to sweep it off. Then it's just heavy.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Kota asks for a ghost story every time he passes. I'm running out. I may have to make some up.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Tome knows every word of every rite. I write them down at night so they don't leave with her.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I bow at Minamino's little roadside shrine every morning. It's small, but it was here first.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: You know it's my birthday? Then the broom gets a day off, and so do I. I'll be at the little roadside shrine, telling it the old tales.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: For my birthday? Grandfather always gave me the first fortune of the year, folded twice. ...I'll fold this away just as carefully.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I tied a charm for good harvests to your gate. Don't tell Tome I used the good paper.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: When I pray for the village, I count every house. Yours is on the list now. Near the top.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I practice the New Year words to the fox statues. They're a tough crowd.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Tome nodded at me today. Just once. I nearly dropped the broom.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I drew a fortune for you this morning. Great blessing. I didn't stack the box. ...Much.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Grandfather said a shrine keeper watches over everyone and no one in particular. I'm bad at the second part.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Kota says I hum when you walk up the shrine path. I told him it's a prayer. It isn't.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Tome says I can't lead my own wedding rite. I said I wrote half the words down. She said that's why.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I keep sweeping the same spot. Three days. Is it always this hard to keep your hands still?

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Good morning. I bowed to your kitchen stove. Tome says every hearth has a god. Yours looked lonely.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Off to sweep. If the fox statues ask, tell them I'm happily married and not taking visitors.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I drew this morning's fortune before you woke. Great blessing. Two days running. Suspicious, I know.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Welcome home. I saved you the last rice cake from the offering. The gods won't mind. Much.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Shall I tell you a ghost story? A short one. With the lamp on, if you like.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: The house is quiet at night. Quieter than the shrine. I like listening to you breathe instead of the wind.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I watered the dry plots before the shrine. A little water for the field god, too.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: The rows by the path were parched, so I gave them a can and a short prayer.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: I filled the coop's feed box. The hens bowed. I'm sure of it.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: The feed's in the coop, from your sack. Offerings for the hens.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Married, and the gravel still needs raking. Some things don't change. I'm glad some things do.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Tome asks after you every morning. Then she asks after the field. In that order, she says.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Oh! This is perfect. I'll share a little with the gods. A very little.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: How kind! Thank you, I'll enjoy this.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Oh, thank you. I'll find a place for it.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Ah... that's a bit much for me. Thank you anyway.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: A stone? I sweep these off the steps every day!

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Another? Even the gods only take one offering a day.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: An omamori from another shrine! Look at this stitching. I'll keep it in the alcove and study it.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: You cooked this? It smells like a festival. Thank you!

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Still warm! I'll eat it on the shrine step.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: A dish! Thank you, that's my supper.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Oh... it's a little heavy for me. I'm sorry.
